probe.implementation: native guard below every two-argument sector write; read T40/S0 and require exact sealed 1581 name, ID 65, structure bytes and L65B marker

real_product_link.projection_note: The hard linker assertion rejected the candidate before the final footprint audit; reserve follows the measured 258-byte overlay-start displacement with unchanged overlay size.

probe.runtime_cost: one additional T40/S0 F011 read for each two-argument physical sector write

mount_token_cache_assessment.native_token: exact five-byte D68B-D68F hypervisor-mounted-image token only
mount_token_cache_assessment.m65d_identity: canonical name plus exact ID plus fresh Lisp latch generation; not present in the native token
mount_token_cache_assessment.compile_path: compile-string uses the two-argument %disk-write-sector directly for every fixed-slot sector and bypasses the M65D transaction latch
mount_token_cache_assessment.capture_boundary: native capture reads D68B-D68F only; it neither reads nor owns a classified T40/S0 header, and the fixed-slot caller has arbitrary target-sector scratch at capture time
mount_token_cache_assessment.size_effect: classifying once instead of once per sector reduces I/O frequency but does not remove the single 177-byte resident classifier; a cache also needs validity, product flag and invalidation logic
mount_token_cache_assessment.trust_boundary: accepting a caller-supplied product bit would let the bypassing path assert its own authorization; making M65D classification authoritative requires a new primitive/bytecode transaction seam and belongs to the 1.1-M structural repair
mount_token_cache_assessment.rejection_reason: The proposed cached bit has no trusted classified value at the native two-argument capture boundary and cannot eliminate the resident classifier that caused the capacity failure.

decision: No debit requested and no product promotion. The v1.0.1 native guard is structurally deferred to 1.1-M unless the owner separately authorizes a different release scope.
